1.e4 c5 2.Nc3 e6 3.g3.strategy: The slow, closed plan: the bishop will go to g2 to bear on the long diagonal and the centre, with the knight on c3 already covering d5. Against 2...e6 it allows ...d5 at once, since the e6 pawn supports that strike, which takes much of the sting out of White's set-up.
1.e4 c5 2.Nc3 e6 3.g3.name: Sicilian Defence: Closed

1.e4 c5 2.Nc3 e6 3.f4.strategy: The Grand Prix set-up: the f-pawn claims kingside space and the e5 square, preparing a direct attack on the king. Against 2...e6, though, Black has ...d5 ready at once, so White's plan has to prove itself against an immediate strike at the centre.

1.e4 c5 2.Nc3 e6 3.Nge2.strategy: Keeps White's options open: the f-pawn and the g-pawn both stay free, and d4 can still be played with a knight recapture. The knight on e2 is passive and blocks the king's bishop, and the set-up is not very challenging for Black.

1.e4 c5 2.Nc3 e6 3.f4 Nc6.strategy: Develops the knight and eyes d4 and e5, keeping ...d5 ready, which the e6 pawn already supports. Black spends no time on a kingside commitment, because the strike in the centre is the answer to White's attacking set-up.

1.e4 c5 2.Nc3 e6 3.g3 d5.strategy: Strikes in the centre before White's bishop has reached g2 and so spoils the closed plan: the e6 pawn supports the push. White's e4 pawn is attacked at once and defended only by the knight.
1.e4 c5 2.Nc3 e6 3.g3 d5.name: Sicilian Defence: Closed, Korchnoi Defence

1.e4 c5 2.Nc3 e6 3.Nge2 a6.strategy: A flexible waiting move that takes b5 from White's pieces and prepares the queenside expansion ...b5. Black keeps every set-up open, including the knight's best square, and spends a tempo on a useful move against a White set-up that is not very threatening.
